public_rationale: The November 4, 2023 review surveys AGI definitions involving typical human cognitive tasks, learning and economically valuable work [e1]. It does not measure how widely those definitions were accepted around February 2022 [e1]. It therefore establishes neither broad agreement that ordinary-human performance was insufficient nor substantial contemporary disagreement with that requirement [e1].
limitations: The later review provides historical definitions, not a representative measurement of February 2022 views [e1].
It does not establish whether the field endorsed Marcus's proposed criteria [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Around early 2022, before LLM euphoria, the field assumed AGI meant more than beating ordinary humans.

statement.excerpt: 18 months ago, before the LLM euphoria, we all took for granted that AGI wasn’t just about beating ordinary humans.
statement.document_title: No, Virginia, AGI is not imminent

from_speaker: AGI wasn’t just about beating ordinary humans
our_interpretation: Eighteen months before the post places the observation around February 2022.
I read we all as a claim of broad agreement in the AI field, not literal unanimity among every researcher.
The proposed agreement concerns requirements beyond outperforming ordinary humans, such as stronger reliability, resourcefulness, or specialist capabilities.
Publication of Marcus's criteria or willingness to host his bet would establish attention to those criteria, not field-wide acceptance.
criteria.support_condition: Representative contemporaneous statements, surveys, or documented discussion establish broad early-2022 agreement that ordinary-human performance was insufficient for AGI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporaneous evidence shows that ordinary-human general capability was widely accepted as sufficient, or that the claimed shared requirement was substantially disputed.
